Agent UUIDs are minted in the agent registry when the agent is registered and are only copied into PREMIS (DPM81). Element order (Placement and file model)
Element order. The PREMIS 3.0 schema fixes the entity sequence: objects, then events, then agents, then rights. Within each, elements carried from the predecessor keep their place, and the elements a version adds follow them (DPM4), so that each version's file begins with its predecessor's elements, entity by entity. Within the elements one version adds: objects by intellectual entity, then representations, then files in logical-path order, a published PDF (which has no logical path, DPM40) immediately before the master derived from it; events in chronological order; agents in order of first reference. A relationship added to an existing object follows that object's existing relationships (DPM4). The order carries no semantics; it exists so that two correct writers produce comparable files, and so that a version's additions can be checked as an extension of its predecessor.

Element order (Placement and file model)
Element order. The PREMIS 3.0 schema fixes the entity sequence: objects, then events, then agents, then rights. Within each, elements carried from the predecessor keep their place, and the elements a version adds follow them (DPM4), so that each version's file begins with its predecessor's elements, entity by entity. Within the elements one version adds: objects by intellectual entity, then representations, then files in logical-path order, a published PDF (which has no logical path, DPM40) immediately before the master derived from it; events in chronological order; agents in order of first reference. A relationship added to an existing object follows that object's existing relationships (DPM4). The order carries no semantics; it exists so that two correct writers produce comparable files, and so that a version's additions can be checked as an extension of its predecessor.

Any source change regenerates every derived file

As soon as anything changes for a document (a new language arrives, or a source file changes), everything the pipeline produced for it is thrown away and made again: the PDF/A masters, their validation and quality reports, and the generated metadata (§4.4, §10). A later section (§5.1) says the opposite: files whose source has not changed are not converted again. Workflow Documentation v2.5 thus contradicts itself.

A new version adds only what is new. When a new language is published, the version adds that language's source files, the PDF/A master made from its published PDF, and the master's reports. The published PDF is not kept: it is only described in PREMIS, as the source the master was made from. The languages already held are left alone. A master is replaced only when its published PDF changes in DOL, or when it is reconverted on purpose (a master reconversion version).

The package follows the "rebuild everything" rule. The Spanish published PDF never changed in DOL, yet its master was made again when French was added (v2) and again when English was added (v3); the French master was made again in v3. Each new master is identical to the one before except for its internal timestamps and document ID. The quality and validation reports were regenerated each time, and so was the DOL metadata extract. The repository now stores three copies of the Spanish master and two of the French, each a separate file that PREMIS must describe and that has to be kept forever.

Rebuild only what a change actually affects: outputs made from a new or changed source are produced again; everything else is carried forward unchanged from the previous version. Resolve the contradiction between §4.4 and §5.1.

No-change test on regenerated outputs

Just before storing, the pipeline (PoC 9) compares what it is about to store with what the repository already holds, file by file, by path and checksum (§5.1). If everything is identical, it creates no new version and records "no change" (STEP_9_OCFL_NO_CHANGE).

A new version is created only when there is a reason for one: the reason the document was picked up from DOL, recorded as its selection basis (a new document, a new language, a revised document, a metadata change…). If nothing has changed in DOL (for example, a document re-issued with none of its languages changed), no version is created (Excluded facts). Whether a version is needed is decided on the sources, comparing the published PDF's checksum, not the master's, before the final comparison (Consequential changes).

The package contains no run in which nothing changed, so the no-change test itself is not exercised. It shows that a regenerated file is never byte-identical to its predecessor, even from the same source. The Spanish master was produced three times from the same published PDF (QA report source SHA-512 9986bff4… in v1–v3) and has a different SHA-512 each time (031ad184…, c3713849…, 5addec12…). The files are the same size and differ only in the modification date (PDF info and XMP) and the document ID: 13 bytes between v1 and v2, 17 between v2 and v3. The French master shows the same in v3 (16 bytes). The DOL metadata extract differs between versions only in its extraction time (extracted_utc). The no-change test therefore works only if nothing is regenerated in a run without changes. Whether that holds, in particular whether the DOL metadata extract is taken afresh in every run, is not shown by the package and should be confirmed with the developer.

Decide whether anything has changed by looking at what comes from DOL before anything is built: the source files and published PDFs, by path and checksum, as PoC 1 already does (§4.3), and the DOL metadata by its content, not its extraction time. Keep the final comparison before storing as a safety check.

PREMIS is projected from run evidence

In each run, the pipeline (PoC 6) writes a new PREMIS file from scratch, built from the records that run kept of its files and events (§4.10). Separately, §4.4 deletes those records whenever a source changes, so the records of earlier runs are no longer there to draw on.

PREMIS is a running record of the object's whole history. Each new version takes the PREMIS file of the version before and adds its own entries; nothing already recorded is removed or rewritten (DPM2–DPM4, DPM117).

Each version's PREMIS file describes only its own run. None of v1's 6 events appears in v2, and none of v2's 11 appears in v3: every event carries a new identifier and describes the latest run. Because files are identified by their path, the Spanish master keeps the same identifier in all three versions, but each time it describes the latest copy only (SHA-512 031ad184… in v1, c3713849… in v2, 5addec12… in v3); the earlier copies, still held in the repository, are no longer described. Someone reading the latest PREMIS file would not learn when or how the Spanish master was first made, or that two earlier copies exist. That history survives only in the PREMIS files of the earlier versions.
PoC 6 opens the PREMIS file of the latest stored version and adds the new version's entries to it. The records of earlier runs are then no longer needed.

Version storage: self-contained or forward-delta

Every new version is stored as a complete, self-contained copy: its folder holds every file of the document, including those that have not changed since the version before (§5.1, §5.2, §10, §13). A version folder missing an unchanged file is described as a defect.

Each version's folder holds only the files that are new in that version. An unchanged file is stored once, in the version that first added it, and later versions point to it through the OCFL inventory; nothing is stored twice ("forward-delta"; The OCFL inventory; Example 2).

Half-way to what is proposed. The storage itself works as proposed: each file is stored once, and a file unchanged since an earlier version is not stored again but points back to the earlier copy. Across the three versions there are 45 files (10 in v1, 15 in v2, 20 in v3), of which 42 are stored: the Spanish DOCX is stored only in v1, and the French DOCX only in v2. Because every run rebuilds the masters and reports (W01), they come out with new bytes even when their source is unchanged, and are stored again: the Spanish master three times, the French master twice.

Each transfer package (a BagIt "bag") carries a label file, bag-info.txt, identifying it (§4.11). There, the External-Identifier is the JOB_ID and the Internal-Sender-Identifier the pipeline's internal folder UUID. The bag follows BagIt 0.97.

The label file says unambiguously what the bag is and what it belongs to, and the ingest side checks it before storing anything, holding the bag if any value disagrees (DPM2, DPM3, Example 1). External-Identifier: the UUID of this transfer (the SIP), so that each bag is identified uniquely. Internal-Sender-Identifier: the JOB_ID, the document in ODRNS's own terms.
